info.name: DeskNu API Documentation
info.description: REST API for DeskNu — ticket creation and lifecycle, routing, SLA, notifications, and administration. Backs the web, mobile and any third-party clients equally; this document is the contract.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
Token-based authentication shared by the web, mobile and third-party
clients. All endpoints here are unauthenticated except /auth/logout,
/auth/me and the email verification resend endpoint, which require a
Bearer token obtained from /auth/login or /auth/register.

request.description:
Creates a new Customer-role account and an associated customer
profile, then returns a Bearer token. A verification email is
queued automatically.

Exchanges email/password credentials for a Sanctum Bearer token.
Pass a `device_name` so multiple tokens (web, iOS, Android) can be
managed and revoked independently per device.

Second step of `/auth/login` for an account that has two-factor authentication
on. Send the `challenge_token` from the login response plus either the 6-digit
code from the authenticator app (`code`) or one unused recovery code
(`recovery_code`). Wrong codes count toward the same lockout as wrong passwords.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "Validation failed.", "errors": {"code": ["The code is incorrect or has expired."]}}
{"success": false, "message": "Too many failed sign-in attempts. This account is locked for another 15 minutes."}

item.name: Users
item.description:
Internal staff accounts (agents, senior agents, department managers,
administrators). Customer accounts are managed under the Customers
group instead.

request.description:
Creates an internal account (agent, senior agent, department
manager or administrator) with a single role and optional
department memberships.

Users may update their own name/phone/timezone; only holders of
`users.update` may change another user's record or flip
`is_active`.

Soft-deletes the account and revokes all of its API tokens.
An administrator cannot delete their own account.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."}

request.description:
Replaces the user's role assignments with the given list.
Requires `roles.manage`.

Clears the lockout from too many failed sign-in attempts, so the person can try
again straight away. Requires `users.update`.

For someone who lost their phone and their recovery codes: switches two-factor off
and signs them out everywhere, so they sign in with their password and can set it
up again. Requires `users.update`; you cannot reset your own.

Lets an administrator (`users.impersonate`) act as another user in the
same tenant to see exactly what they see. Returns a short-lived Bearer
token for that user; the administrator's own token is untouched, so the
client can switch back by discarding this one (`POST /auth/logout` with
it). Not allowed on yourself, inactive users, other administrators, or
from inside an impersonation session. Every use is written to the audit
log as `user.impersonated`.

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Now logged in as the selected user.", "data": {"user": {"id": 5}, "token": "2|abc...", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_at": "2026-10-09T20:00:00+00:00"}}
{"success": false, "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."}

item.name: Roles & Permissions
item.description:
The 5 built-in roles (Administrator, Department Manager, Senior Agent,
Agent, Customer) cover the standard workforce shape; additional
custom roles can be created here and assigned any subset of the
permissions listed by GET /permissions. The Administrator and
Customer roles cannot be deleted.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."}

item.name: Customers
item.description:
Customer profiles. Every customer is backed by a `User` record with
the `Customer` role; this resource manages the additional profile
fields (company, customer type) layered on top of it.

request.description:
Creates a User with the Customer role plus its Customer profile in
a single call, for support staff onboarding a customer by hand.
For self-service signup, use POST /auth/register instead.

Downloads a JSON copy of everything held about this customer (profile, tickets,
messages, attachment names, emails sent to them) to answer a data-access request.
Internal staff notes are left out. Requires `customers.export`.

**Irreversible.** Anonymizes the customer everywhere their identity is stored (account,
customer record, audit entries, the inbound-email log) and signs them out. With
`redact_content` (the default) it also removes the text of their tickets, every message
and all attachments; with `false` the ticket text is kept for your records and only the
person stops being identifiable. Requires `customers.erase`, and the customer's email
typed back as confirmation.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "Validation failed.", "errors": {"confirm_email": ["The email does not match this customer."]}}

item.name: Ticket Messages
item.description:
Customer messages, agent replies and internal notes on a ticket.
Internal notes are never returned to a customer: this is enforced by
excluding them from the query entirely for any caller without the
tickets.view_internal_notes permission, not just by hiding a field.

formdata.value: Thanks for reaching out — can you share a screenshot of the error?

request.description:
Customers always post as `customer_message`. Staff post as
`agent_reply` by default, or `internal_note` when `is_internal`
is true and they hold tickets.view_internal_notes — a customer
sending `is_internal` has it silently ignored, never honored.

item.name: Ticket Attachments
item.description:
Files are validated on MIME type, extension and size at upload time
(see StoreTicketMessageRequest / this controller's own rules) and
are never served directly from public storage — every download goes
through the authorization check in TicketAttachmentPolicy, which
also denies customers access to a file attached to an internal note.

request.description:
For a file attached directly to the ticket rather than a specific
message. To attach a file to a message, use the `attachments[]`
field on POST /tickets/{ticket}/messages instead.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "You do not have permission to perform this action."}

item.name: Categories
item.description:
Ticket categories and subcategories. A "subcategory" is simply another
row with parent_id set — see the architecture docs for why this
replaces a separate child-categories table.

request.description:
Returns top-level categories with their children eager-loaded.
Use filter[parent_id]=null to explicitly list only root categories.

Soft-deletes the category and cascades to its subcategories.
Tickets already in this category keep their category_id.

item.name: Statuses
item.description:
The seven built-in statuses (Open, In Progress, Pending, Escalated,
Resolved, Closed, Reopened) drive the ticket status workflow (see
docs/ticket-workflow.md) and are matched by slug, not id — additional
statuses can be added here for labeling/reporting but will not
automatically participate in transition validation.

request.description: Refuses to delete a status that is currently in use by any ticket.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "This status is in use by existing tickets and cannot be deleted."}

item.name: Priorities
item.description:
Ticket priorities. `level` is a numeric ordering used by routing
rules and reporting (higher = more urgent).

request.description: Refuses to delete a priority that is currently in use by any ticket.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "This priority is in use by existing tickets and cannot be deleted."}

item.name: Routing
item.description:
Ticket routing rules, evaluated in `priority` order (lowest first)
against every newly-created ticket. See docs/routing.md for the full
condition/action schema and worked examples.

body.raw: {"name":"Route billing category to Billing dept","description":"Eius et animi quos velit et.","priority":10,"is_active":true,"stop_processing":true,"conditions":[{"field":"category_id","operator":"=","value":3}],"actions":[{"type":"assign_department","value":2}]}

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Routing rule created successfully.", "data": {"id": 3, "name": "Route billing category to Billing dept"}}

item.name: SLA
item.description:
SLA policies define first-response and resolution deadlines. The
most specific match wins when a ticket's SLA is calculated: priority
+ department, falling back to a department-less default for that
priority — see CalculateSlaAction and docs/ticket-workflow.md.

body.raw: {"name":"VIP Customer SLA","description":"Eius et animi quos velit et.","priority_id":4,"department_id":2,"business_hours_id":16,"first_response_minutes":15,"resolution_minutes":120,"business_hours_only":false,"is_default":false,"is_active":true}

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "SLA policy created successfully.", "data": {"id": 5, "name": "VIP Customer SLA"}}

item.name: Notifications
item.description:
Every user manages their own notification preferences — there is no
admin override of another user's preferences, since they describe a
personal inbox choice, not a permission.

request.description:
Any event key without an explicit preference row is enabled by
default (opt-out model) and simply won't appear here until set.

Upserts one or more (channel, event_key) preferences for the
authenticated user.

body.raw: {"subject":"We received your ticket {ticket_number}","body":"Hi {customer_name}, your ticket has been created...","is_active":true}

item.name: Reports
item.description:
Aggregate reporting. These run live queries rather than against a
pre-aggregated table — acceptable at the data volumes a support
desk accumulates, but the first thing to revisit if that changes.

request.description: Open ticket counts grouped by status, priority and department.

Breach rates for first response and resolution across all
tickets with a calculated SLA.
Resolved-ticket counts per agent, most active first.

item.name: Audit Logs
item.description:
System-wide, read-only audit trail. Distinct from a ticket's own
activity feed (GET /tickets/{ticket}/activities) — this covers every
auditable action across the whole application for compliance review:
login, ticket create/assign/status-change, customer/user creation,
role changes, API credential and webhook lifecycle events, and
platform-admin tenant actions. There is currently no billing-change
endpoint for a platform admin to alter an existing tenant's
subscription/plan, so that action from section 42 has nothing to log
yet.

item.name: Settings
item.description:
System-wide configuration key/value pairs. Anyone authenticated can
read the subset marked is_public (e.g. a "support hours" display
string); the full set, and all writes, require settings.manage.

request.description:
Send a colour as `null` to go back to its default. Only the colours you send
change. A primary colour white text could not be read on, or a sidebar colour
too light for the sidebar's text, is refused.

Returns every row for this tenant (current and historical),
most recently effective first.

Deactivates any existing active row for the same scope
(`department_id`, or the tenant's global default when omitted)
and inserts this as the new active one — the previous row is kept
for history, not deleted.

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Ticket number setting created successfully.", "data": {"id": 2, "prefix": "ACME", "is_active": true}}

item.name: API Credentials
item.description:
Key+secret pairs a tenant issues to its own backend/CRM/chat widget
to call the Integration API (see docs under "Integration API —
Customers/Tickets"). Scoped to the caller's own tenant like
everything else here; a credential's secret is only ever visible in
the response to the single store()/rotate() call that generated it.

request.description:
The secret is returned exactly once, here — it is hashed at
rest and cannot be recovered afterward. Store it securely; if
it's lost, rotate the credential for a new one.

item.name: Update an API credential's name or scopes

request.description:
Issues a brand-new secret for the same key; the old secret
stops working immediately. Use this instead of revoking +
recreating when only the secret (not the whole credential and
its scopes/history) needs to change.

Immediately and permanently stops this credential from
authenticating. Cannot be undone — issue a new credential
instead of expecting this one to work again.

item.name: Billing
item.description:
A tenant's own view of its subscription — distinct from
Platform\TenantController, which lets a platform administrator see
every tenant's subscription. Moving to a paid plan issues an invoice
with a Razorpay order; the subscription is activated when that invoice
is paid (see InvoiceController and MarkInvoicePaidAction).

request.description:
Includes a `usage` block (one entry per plan-limited feature)
computed live via PlanLimitService — the same service every
resource-creating controller already uses to enforce limits, so
this can never drift from what creation actually allows.

A free plan activates immediately. A paid plan starts a 14-day
trial and issues an invoice for the plan price, with a Razorpay
order to pay it; the subscription is activated once the invoice is
paid. A lapsed subscription (past_due, suspended or expired) gets no
new trial and keeps its lapsed status until that invoice is paid.
Earlier unpaid invoices are voided. If the payment provider
cannot create the order, nothing changes and the request returns 503.

Called by the browser after Razorpay Checkout succeeds. The signature
is checked with the key secret; an unsigned or mismatched payment is
rejected and the invoice stays pending.

item.name: Integration API — Customers
item.description:
Authenticated via X-Api-Key / X-Api-Secret headers (see
ResolveIntegrationTenantContext), not a Sanctum session — for a
tenant's own backend, CRM or chat widget to keep its customer
records in sync with this helpdesk. Every endpoint here is scoped to
the credential's own tenant; there is no cross-tenant visibility no
matter what id is requested.

item.name: Look up a customer by email or external id

request.description:
No password is set — this customer can request one later via
POST /auth/forgot-password if they ever need direct portal
access; most integration-created customers never do.

item.name: Integration API — Lookups
item.description:
The ids a client site needs to fill its "new ticket" form (priority,
department, category dropdowns). Read-only, scoped to the credential's own
tenant, and only active departments/categories are returned. Requires the
tickets.create scope — these exist to build create-ticket requests.

request.description:
Active departments only. Pass the chosen `id` as `department_id` when
creating a ticket. A routing rule on the tenant may still re-route the ticket.

Active categories only. Pass the chosen `id` as `category_id` when
creating a ticket.

item.name: Integration API — Tickets
item.description:
Same credential-based auth as the Customers integration endpoints.
"Reply" and "attachment" actions here are posted on behalf of the
ticket's customer — there is no staff Sanctum session backing this
credential, so there is no agent identity to attribute them to; use
the regular Sanctum-authenticated ticket endpoints for agent-side
actions.

request.description:
The priorities and (active) departments a customer-facing "new
ticket" form can offer. Both are optional on ticket creation; omitted
values fall back to the tenant default priority and routing rules.

Customer messages and agent replies only — internal notes are never
returned. Authors are reduced to a display name (no email or roles).

Membership Plans
item.description:
Public plan catalog for the pricing page and tenant registration's
`plan` field — unauthenticated, read-only, mirrors the public
/tenants/register and /tenants/lookup/{slug} endpoints. Only active
plans are listed; platform administrators manage the full catalog
(including inactive/retired plans) via Platform\MembershipPlanController.

item.name: Platform Administration
item.description:
A single-call overview for the platform admin landing screen —
everything here is a cheap count query, not a report; GET
/platform/tenants already supports filtering/pagination for
anything needing the underlying rows.

request.description:
Immediately blocks every user of this tenant from authenticating
further (ResolveTenantContext rejects any tenant that isn't
active/trial) and from registering new accounts. Existing Sanctum
tokens are not individually revoked — they simply stop working
the next time they hit a tenant-scoped route.

Marks the tenant's `email.sending_domain` as having SPF/DKIM in place.
Only then, and only on a plan above Starter, do the tenant's emails go
out from support@<domain> instead of the platform address.

item.name: Assign a membership plan to a tenant

request.description:
Same rules as the tenant's own plan change: a free plan is active with no
trial, a paid plan starts a 14-day trial. Creates the subscription if the
tenant has none.

Existing subscriptions are unaffected until their next billing
cycle re-evaluates limits — this only changes what NEW
subscriptions, and PlanLimitService's live checks for all
subscriptions, see going forward.

item.name: Tenant Registration
item.description:
Self-service signup for a brand-new organization, distinct from
/auth/register (which adds a Customer to an *existing* tenant's
helpdesk). This flow creates the tenant itself, its first
subscription and its first user — the Tenant Owner, who lands with
the full-access "Administrator" role for that tenant only.

request.description:
Creates the tenant, subscribes it to the given plan (the free
Starter plan if omitted), provisions its default roles/ticket
statuses/priorities, and creates the owner account. Starter-plan
signups are active immediately; any paid plan starts a 14-day
trial (no payment is collected here — billing integration is out
of scope for this API).

item.name: Look up an organization by slug

request.description:
Used by login/registration clients to confirm a tenant slug
exists and is currently accepting sign-ins before prompting for
credentials. Deliberately returns only non-sensitive fields.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "No organization found for that identifier."}

item.name: Ticket Tags
item.description:
Free-form labels agents put on tickets ("vip", "refund", "bug") to group and
filter them. Staff only: customers can see tags on their tickets' staff views
nowhere and cannot set them.

request.description:
Replaces the ticket's tags with exactly this list. Tags that don't exist yet

item.name: Two-factor authentication
item.description:
Lets a signed-in person protect their own account with an authenticator app
(Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…). Every step
asks for the current password again, so a stolen session token alone can't
switch protection on or off. Wrong passwords and wrong codes here count toward
the same lockout as at sign-in.

request.description:
Returns a new secret and the `otpauth://` link to show as a QR code. Two-factor is
not active yet: call `/auth/two-factor/confirm` with a code from the app first.

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "Scan the code, then confirm with a code from your app.", "data": {"secret": "JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP", "otpauth_url": "otpauth://totp/DeskNu:me%40example.com?secret=JBSWY3DPEHPK3PXP&issuer=DeskNu"}}
{"success": false, "message": "Two-factor authentication is already on. Turn it off first to set it up again."}

request.description:
Confirms setup with the first 6-digit code from the app. Returns the recovery
codes **once**; each works a single time if the phone is lost.

response.body: {"success": false, "message": "Validation failed.", "errors": {"code": ["The code is incorrect or has expired."]}}

request.description: Replaces all recovery codes. The old ones stop working.

response.body: {"success": true, "message": "New recovery codes created. The old ones no longer work.", "data": {"recovery_codes": ["ab12c-d34ef"]}}

item.name: Webhooks
item.description:
Tenant-configured HTTP callbacks for ticket lifecycle events (see
Webhook::EVENTS). Every delivery is signed with the webhook's own
secret via an X-Webhook-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
JSON body) so the receiving endpoint can verify it actually came
from this platform.

request.description:
The secret is returned exactly once, here — it is encrypted at
rest and this is the only response that ever includes it in
plain text. Use it to verify the X-Webhook-Signature header on
each delivery.

item.name: List a webhook's recent delivery attempts
Send a test event to a webhook

request.description:
Delivers a synthetic `webhook.test` event to this webhook's URL
right away (not queued, never retried) so its endpoint and
signature verification can be checked without waiting for a
real ticket event. The attempt is still recorded as an ordinary
delivery, visible via GET /webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries.

Issues a brand-new secret for this webhook; the old one no
longer verifies X-Webhook-Signature on any future delivery. Use
this instead of deleting and recreating the webhook when only
the secret needs to change.
